title: The Great Bun Photo
markdown:
The Great Spring Fair buzzed with happy sounds. Wren the robin puffed her chest. “Theo, the awards are today. I made my best feather extra shiny.”

Theo the mouse wiggled his whiskers. “And I have my shiniest acorn. But I’m also excited for Aunt Olive’s tasty buns.”

Aunt Olive smiled, warm as sunshine. “Don’t worry about prizes, dears,” she hummed, bustling by with a basket. “There will be warm sugary treats for everyone.” Wren and Theo imagined sweet cinnamon smells trailing after her like a ribbon.

Iola Bellows, a friendly lamb with a camera, trotted over. “Winners,” she bleated. “It’s time for the official photo.”

Wren and Theo, who had won shiny ribbons, lined up with a happy group. Iola adjusted her spectacles. “Look at the camera, please.”

Wren’s eyes flickered sideways. “Oh my,” she whispered. “Aunt Olive’s buns smell extra delicious.” A rabbit nudged a badger, and they all leaned toward the picnic basket.

Iola sighed softly. “No, no, please. Look at me. At the camera.” She tried again. “One, two, three, hold that pose.” But the rabbit admired a bun, bumping the badger, who bumped a squirrel. They tumbled like fluffy pillows, all looking at the yummy food.

“Oh dearie me,” Iola said, her ears drooping. “This is lively.” She waited. Wren, Theo, the rabbit, the badger, and the squirrel looked serious. Iola counted, “One, two, three.” Click.

She looked at the screen. They were not looking at her. Every nose and eye pointed past her shoulder. Iola peeked. There, piled high on a checkered blanket, were Aunt Olive’s famous buns, smelling like pure happiness. And reflected in Iola’s camera lens, shining brightly, were those glorious buns.

Wren giggled like tiny bells. Theo quivered with delight. “Miss Bellows,” Wren chirped, “the buns look beautiful in your camera.”

Aunt Olive chuckled. “Perhaps the best prize isn’t a ribbon, but a picture of what makes everyone happy.”

Iola looked at her screen, then at the happy faces. She had wanted a neat photo, but this was a picture of pure joy. She smiled her gentle lamb smile. “You know what? A picture with the buns is a truly magnificent winner’s photograph.”

She raised her camera again, pointing it at Aunt Olive’s blanket. “Everyone, turn and look at Aunt Olive’s wonderful buns.”

With happy squeaks and chirps, everyone turned. Iola clicked again. The screen showed a glorious sight: Wren, Theo, the rabbit, the badger, and the squirrel, their eyes shining with delight, with the magnificent buns reflected before them like a treasure. It was not the neat photo Iola had planned, but it was, in its own whimsical way, the most perfect photograph of all.
characters: Wren (shiny-feather robin), Theo (acorn-proud mouse), Aunt Olive (sugary-bun baker)
author: StoryGen Community
